title: Deep OFFSET paging on a sort key that is not unique
prompt: Admin order grid with @Take = 50. Users page deep: @Skip of 100k to 500k is common for 'Shipped' (about 25M rows),
and the last-page button sends @Skip = total - 50. Typical deep pages take 6 to 40 s. The plan scans or sorts
millions of wide rows before it discards @Skip of them. Support staff report that rows appear twice or go missing
when they page through batch-imported orders, which share OrderDate values. The grid API takes Skip and Take today.
A change to a cursor API is possible, but it is a separate frontend project.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).
baseline_sql: SELECT o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Status, o.TotalAmount, o.SalesChannel, o.PromoCode,
JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
OFFSET @Skip ROWS FETCH NEXT @Take ROWS ONLY;

correct_families.description: Page over a narrow ordered index of keys with a unique tiebreaker, then fetch the wide columns for the page only, in the same order.

all: OrderDate desc\s*,\s*\w+\.OrderID desc.*rows only\s*\).*OrderDate desc\s*,\s*\w+\.OrderID desc

reference_sql: ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC, o.OrderID DESC
OFFSET @Skip ROWS FETCH NEXT @Take ROWS ONLY
SELECT o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Status, o.TotalAmount, o.SalesChannel, o.PromoCode,
JOIN qe.Orders    o ON o.OrderID = k.OrderID
JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
ORDER BY k.OrderDate DESC, k.OrderID DESC;

traps.why: Keyset paging needs the last key seen and cannot jump to page N. The grid API sends Skip and Take, so this is an interface change, not a replacement.
traps.told_apart_by: The existing callers pass @Skip and @Take and have no last key to send.
example_sql: SELECT TOP (@Take) o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Status, o.TotalAmount, o.SalesChannel, o.PromoCode,
JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC, o.OrderID DESC;

traps.why: The order of a CTE is not kept. Without the same ORDER BY on the outer query the page rows come back in any order.
traps.told_apart_by: Any page: the 50 rows are right but their order is not guaranteed.
example_sql: ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC, o.OrderID DESC
OFFSET @Skip ROWS FETCH NEXT @Take ROWS ONLY
SELECT o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Status, o.TotalAmount, o.SalesChannel, o.PromoCode,
JOIN qe.Orders    o ON o.OrderID = k.OrderID
JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID;

traps.why: With ORDER BY OrderDate alone, tied rows can change places between calls. The duplicate and missing rows stay.
example_sql: OFFSET @Skip ROWS FETCH NEXT @Take ROWS ONLY
SELECT o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Status, o.TotalAmount, o.SalesChannel, o.PromoCode,
JOIN qe.Orders    o ON o.OrderID = k.OrderID
JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID

traps.why: ROW_NUMBER with a range filter still numbers every row up to the page.
example_sql: SELECT t.OrderID, t.OrderDate, t.Status, t.TotalAmount, t.SalesChannel, t.PromoCode,
FROM (SELECT o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Status, o.TotalAmount, o.SalesChannel, o.PromoCode,
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC, o.OrderID DESC) AS rn
JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID

min_improvement.basis: A deep page reads @Skip narrow index rows instead of sorting or scanning millions of wide rows.

key.reference_notes: OrderID as a tiebreaker gives one of the orders the original allowed, and it fixes the reported duplicates. The Customers join can move after the paging because Orders.CustomerID is NOT NULL with a trusted foreign key.
